subject: Re: BlueHarbor live ingest failures — SDK v2.4.1 streaming incompatibility
messages:
From: BlueHarbor Integrations <integrations@blueharbor.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: BlueHarbor SRE <sre@blueharbor.io>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Live ingest errors / p99 latency since SDK v2.4.1

Mina,

We started seeing elevated 5xx rates and p99 token latency on our live ingest stream around 08:50 PDT after upgrading to Redwood client SDK v2.4.1 (the auto-update bundle). Error rate jumped to ~6% (previously <0.2%) and the stream stalls intermittently for a few seconds before resuming. We rely on continuous streaming for our checkout flow — this is impacting customer sessions.

Attached are a short log extract and a packet capture from the incident window.

Key notes:
- Impact: ~3% of checkout requests observed as aborted, p99 token latency ~2.3 s (normally 120 ms)
- Repro: appears correlated to client reconnects + keep-alive reuse over persistent connections
- Workaround tried: rolling back to SDK v2.3.8 on a small canary reduced failures but not eliminated them

We need immediate help: what can we roll back or patch? We can open a maintenance window if needed.

— Evan Park, BlueHarbor Integrations
attachments: repro_log_snippet.txt, packet_trace.pcap

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@blueharbor.io>
Cc: BlueHarbor SRE <sre@blueharbor.io>, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Live ingest errors / p99 latency since SDK v2.4.1

Thanks Evan — receiving this and prioritising. I've looped in engineering (Jonas) and CS (Marissa).

Immediate plan:
- Engineering will triage the packet capture and logs to identify whether this is an SDK regression or a server-side interaction change.
- If SDK v2.4.1 is the culprit we'll recommend a rollback and provide a patched release.
- We'll aim to provide a mitigation (canary rollback + throttling) within 2 hours and a postmortem and next steps within 24 hours.

Can you confirm the percentage of customers still on the auto-update channel and whether you have a maintenance window tonight (PDT)?

Mina
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Evan Park <evan.park@blueharbor.io>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Live ingest errors / p99 latency since SDK v2.4.1

Mina / Evan — quick initial triage below after reviewing the PCAP and the repro logs. I attached a short trace and a proposed rollback note.

What I see:
- The client is using HTTP/1.1 persistent connections; when chunked responses are streamed back and the client performs a reconnect the dechunker in v2.4.1 can mis-order pseudo-headers under our legacy framing code path. That mis-ordering leads to the server runtime rejecting the frame as malformed intermittently which surfaces as 503/502 and results in the transient stall while the client retries.
- The pattern aligns with keep-alive reuse + small chunk sizes (~512B) from the client side. I can reproduce locally with our test harness when I force the same connection reuse pattern.

Immediate actions I recommend (start now):
1) Push a targeted canary rollback: instruct affected BlueHarbor machines to pin SDK v2.3.8 for the ingress pool. Rolling back should drop error rate to baseline.
2) Ship a hotfix branch: replace the legacy dechunker fast-path with the safer reassembly path we validated in CI (PR ready: INF-9876).
3) Add a temporary server-side tolerant fallback that accepts out-of-order pseudo-headers for 24 hrs while we roll customers.

Attachments: repro_log_snippet.txt (subset), packet_trace.pcap, rollback_instructions.md

I will start the rollback playbook now; will report back within the hour with metrics.

— Jonas Weber
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@blueharbor.io>
Cc: BlueHarbor SRE <sre@blueharbor.io>, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 10:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Live ingest errors / p99 latency since SDK v2.4.1

Evan — quick update and proposed timeline.

What we're doing now:
- Jonas has started the canary rollback instructions against your staging ingress pool (per attachment). Early telemetry from the canary nodes shows error rate falling to ~0.4% and p99 latency trending down.
- We're simultaneously deploying the server-side tolerant fallback to keep live traffic stable during customer-level rollbacks.

Next 2 hours:
- Full rollback across affected ingress machines (target: 60 minutes to complete)
- Run smoke tests, validate checkout flows for a 15-minute steady window
- If rollback stabilises, we'll create a hotfix release and schedule an orchestrated client patch (v2.4.1->v2.4.1-p1) with a test rollout.

Business ask / executive note:
- BlueHarbor has a measurable impact on revenue — they'll likely expect a goodwill credit for the incident window. Can CS/sales confirm approach (percentage credit, timing) while we stabilise? Marissa / Ben please advise and loop in finance if needed.

Links: HubSpot case https://hubspot.example/deal/BLUEHARBOR-3421, Jira INF-9876 (fix branch + CI green).

Mina

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Evan Park <evan.park@blueharbor.io>
Date: Wed, 30 Aug 2028 01:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Live ingest errors / p99 latency since SDK v2.4.1

Quick closure note and next steps — summary for execs:

What happened: SDK v2.4.1 introduced a regression in the dechunker fast-path that causes out-of-order pseudo-headers on persistent HTTP/1.1 connections when clients frequently reconnect. This surfaced as intermittent 5xx and token stalls for BlueHarbor.

Actions completed:
- Canary rollback to v2.3.8 executed and validated (error rate reduced to baseline).
- Server-side tolerant fallback deployed as a short-term mitigation.
- Hotfix branch (INF-9876) merged; patch build scheduled for release tomorrow morning UTC.
- CS proposed a 10% credit for the incident day; legal/finance review in motion. DocuSign for the credit memo has been generated: https://docusign.example/packet/BLUEHARBOR-CREDIT-3421

Open items:
- Postmortem and root cause analysis (owner: Jonas) due EOD tomorrow.
- Coordinate customer patch rollout and verify auto-update channel flags (owner: Mina).
- Finance to approve final credit amount and timing (owner: Marissa/Finance).

Ben
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
